title: Mammoth extend André Tourigny, sign former Canucks coach Adam Foote as assistant
content:
The Utah Mammoth have signed coach André Tourigny to a multi-year contract extension, in addition to bringing aboard former Vancouver Canucks coach Adam Foote as an assistant coach on Tourigny’s staff.

According to The Athletic’s Pierre LeBrun, Tourigny had one year left on his current contract. The team also gave out a multi-year extension to assistant coach Blaine Forsythe. Per club policy, financial terms were not disclosed.

Tourigny will enter his third season behind the Mammoth bench this fall. He also helmed the franchise during its final three years as the Arizona Coyotes before its relocation to Utah ahead of the 2024-25 NHL season. Tourigny has an all-time NHL coaching record of 170-195-45.

Tourigny reached the playoffs for the first time with the Mammoth in 2025-26, losing in the first round to the eventual Western Conference-champion Vegas Golden Knights, after guiding them to a fourth-place finish in the Central Division and the first wild-card spot in the Western Conference.

The Quebec native previously worked as an assistant coach with the Ottawa Senators and the Colorado Avalanche, and also spent years coaching in major-junior hockey with the Rouyn-Noranda Huskies, the Halifax Mooseheads and the Ottawa 67’s. Tourigny also won a gold medal with Team ‘Canada as head coach of their IIHF World Championship team in 2023. He also won gold as an assistant coach on staff in 2021.

Foote spent the last four seasons on the Canucks’ coaching staff, including last season as the team’s bench boss. But Foote finished last season with an NHL-worst 25-49-8 record as the Canucks dropped to the bottom of the NHL standings. Foote and his entire staff were dismissed by Vancouver’s new GM Ryan Johnson shortly after he took over.

Forsythe has worked alongside Tourigny since 2023-24, when they were both members of the Coyotes’ franchise. He is in charge of the Mammoth power play, which ranked 18th league-wide in 2025-26, operating at a 20 percent rate.
